When Wang's fiancee is kidnapped by a street gang, he enlists the help of his devoted friend Jack Burton (an unforgetable Kurt Russell). The two soon find themselves caught up in an ongoing battle between good and evil taking place both in and beneath the streets of San Francisco's Chinatown.

description_paragraphs:
Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman star as Rick and Ilsa, two ex-lovers brought back together by fate in Nazi occupied Casablanca. Ilsa's new husband needs out of the country to continue his efforts against the Third Reich, and American ex-pat Rick may be the only one who can aid their escape. And while he's reluctant to risk his nightclub and his life, he's even more torn over the possibility of losing the only woman he's ever truly loved for a second time.
Consistently named one of the finest films ever made, Casablanca lives up to its reputation with its romantic tale fused with tension and humor.

description_paragraphs: Do you love movies and want to find others who can talk endlessly about them? Come join Cinemancy! Each month, a new movie is carefully selected. After the film the audience gathers to discuss themes, characters, plot, and symbolism. Hosted by Isabella Price. Legend Set in a timeless mythical forest inhabited by fairies, goblins, unicorns and mortals, this fantastic story follows a mystical forest dweller, chosen by fate, to undertake a heroic quest. He must save the beautiful Princess Lili and defeat the demonic Lord of Darkness (a perfectly cast Tim Curry), or the world will be plunged into a never-ending ice age. Ridley Scott's fantasy may be the perfect film for Cinemancy. While undeniably beautiful, there's plenty to debate and discuss, including "would you rather: Tom Cruise or Demonic Tim Curry" edition. This is the original theatrical cut with the Tangerine Dream score. Feel free to meet up in the lobby cafe starting at 6:30 if you want to talk movies with your fellow cinephiles.

description_paragraphs: A sleeper hit of the early 1980s, Eating Raoul is a bawdy, gleefully amoral tale of conspicuous consumption. Warhol superstar Mary Woronov and cult legend Paul Bartel (who also directed) portray a prudish married couple who feel put upon by swingers living in their apartment building. One night, by accident, they discover a way to simultaneously rid themselves of the "perverts" down the hall and realize their dream of opening a restaurant. A mix of slapstick and satire, Eating Raoul serves its dark humor with an upbeat attitude and is a great addition to our month of Food and Family at Central Cinema.

description_paragraphs: Seattle Scare Society brings you the perfect movie to prepare you for the holiday chopping shopping season. The Park Plaza Mall just activated the latest in after-hours security; high tech robots sure to keep all the stores safe with (supposedly) non-lethal technology. But when an unfortunate lightning storm strikes the building, these robots go from keeping the peace to causing carnage. It sure would be an unfortunate night for a group of teens to throw a late night party in a furniture store, wouldn't it? Packed with familiar faces for B-movie fans (Dick Miller, Mary Woronov, Paul Bartel), this movie crams more slit throats, lasers, and exploding robots into 77 minutes than most filmmakers can muster in an entire career. Come early for Seattle Scare Society's signature pre-show fun! 7pm - Trailers and Trivia 7:30pm - Feature start time This event does not qualify for Tuesday two-for-one tickets

description_paragraphs: Music maestro David Byrne took inspiration from tabloid headlines to create the only film he's directed, an ode to the extraordinariness of ordinary American life. Byrne is also our on screen host, a visitor to the town of Virgil, Texas, who introduces us to the locals as they prepare for the town's 150th anniversary and the Celebration of Specialness. We meet a local singer who just wants to find his true love, a woman who can't seem to ever get out of bed, and a community leader who really enjoys veggies. Using Talking Heads music to stich together the town's happenings, Byrne creates a loving tapestry of stories, showing his audience that everyday life always has interesting tales beneath the simple surface.
